claims.harm: SockMan mimics a generic I/O framework without its features, remains tightly coupled to Core's P2P send/recv model, and is ill-suited for HTTP or SV2
claims.quote: I believe this is the wrong abstraction level. SockMan is essentially mimicking the behavior of a generic io multiplexing framework (libevent, libuv, etc.), but without the feature-set of those libs.

claims.harm: returning a raw CNode pointer after unlocking m_nodes_mutex risks leaving callers with a dangling pointer if another thread deletes the node
claims.quote: An issue here is that we return a CNode*, unlock m_nodes_mutex, then another thread comes along and deletes the node - leaving the caller with a dangling pointer.

claims.harm: maintaining separate unordered maps to link connection IDs, sockets, and metadata is fragile and prone to getting out of sync
claims.quote: It would seem less fragile to just replace the m_permissions field with a more generic field like std::any m_metadata or std::any m_user_data instead of requiring the application to maintain a separate unordered map and needing to deal with conditions when the map and vector could get out of sync

claims.harm: bind error message string is untranslated
